distinction:d_upc_einheitspatent_buendel.label: Unitary Patent vs. classic European patent (bundle patent)
distinction:d_upc_einheitspatent_buendel.frage: How do the European patent with unitary effect and the classic, nationally validated European patent differ after grant?
rows: Regulations (EU) No 1257/2012 and 1260/2012, UPR, RFeesUPP; practice in the UP Guidelines
Art. 64 ff. EPC and the national law of the designated states (in Germany IntPatÜG, PatG)
Request for unitary effect to the EPO within one month of the mention of grant, registration in the Register (R. 6, 7 UPR); effect retroactive to the mention of grant (Art. 4 UPReg)
Validation state by state: translation, fees and representative under national law (Art. 65 EPC, London Agreement)
Unitary in the participating Member States in which the UPCA was in force at registration (17, or 18 states since 1 September 2024); the generation remains fixed (Art. 18(2) UPReg)
Bundle of national rights in all designated EPC states (up to 39 plus extension and validation states), freely selectable

Transitional period: one full translation for information purposes (Art. 6 TranslReg); none thereafter; in a dispute, translation at the proprietor's expense (Art. 4 TranslReg); compensation of EUR 500 for SMEs and others
Translation of the specification or claims depending on the state and the London Agreement; no compensation
A single fee to the EPO under Art. 2 RFeesUPP (2nd to 20th year EUR 35 to EUR 4,855, total EUR 35,555); six-month grace period with a 50 % surcharge (R. 13 UPR); 15 % reduction for licences of right
National renewal fees per state in national currency with their own time limits and representatives (Art. 141 EPC; § 17 PatG, § 7 PatKostG)

Transfer only for all states, licence also for parts of the territory (Art. 3(2) UPReg); central registration in the Register for unitary patent protection (R. 15, 16 UPR); law applicable to the patent as an object of property under Art. 7 UPReg
Each national part can be transferred separately and is entered in the national register (§ 30 PatG)
Art. 25 to 30 UPCA via the reference in Art. 5(3) UPReg, uniformly for all states
National law (§§ 9 ff. PatG) or, without an opt-out, Art. 25 to 30 UPCA before the UPC
Exclusively the UPC, no opt-out (Art. 3(a), Art. 32 UPCA); actions against EPO decisions also go to the UPC (Art. 32(1)(i) UPCA)
Transitional period until 31 May 2030 (extendable): choice between the UPC and national courts; opt-out possible (Art. 83 UPCA)
Only for all states at once: lapse for non-payment (R. 14 UPR), revocation by the UPC with effect for all states (Art. 34, 65 UPCA); opposition at the EPO still possible
Per state: national revocation action (§ 81 PatG) or UPC revocation action for all Contracting Member States; lapse per state
distinction:d_upc_einheitspatent_buendel.merksatz: One request, one register, one fee, one court – the Unitary Patent replaces the bundle with a single right, but only in the states of its generation.

distinction:d_upc_lokalkammer_zentralkam.label: Local/regional division vs. central division
distinction:d_upc_lokalkammer_zentralkam.frage: Which actions belong before the local or regional division, and which before the central division?
rows: Infringement action, provisional measures, damages, prior use, compensation for licences (Art. 32(1)(a), 32(1)(c), 32(1)(f), 32(1)(g) and 32(1)(h) UPCA); Counterclaim for revocation
Revocation action, declaration of non-infringement (Art. 32(1)(b), 32(1)(d) UPCA); optionally infringement actions against defendants from non-member states; actions against EPO decisions
Place of infringement or defendant's residence (Art. 33(1) UPCA)
IPC class of the patent (Annex II UPCA, R. 17.3 RoP)
Three legally qualified judges; a technically qualified judge on request or in the case of a counterclaim (Art. 8(2) to 8(5) UPCA)
Two legally qualified judges and one technically qualified judge (Art. 8(6) UPCA)
Official language of the host state or an admitted EPO language; language of the patent on request (Art. 49(1) to 49(5) UPCA)
Language of the patent (Art. 49(6) UPCA)
Up to four local divisions per state (DE: Düsseldorf, Hamburg, Mannheim, Munich); Nordic-Baltic regional division
Paris seat; Munich and Milan sections (instead of London)
A pending infringement action draws in the revocation action (Art. 33(4) UPCA); options in the case of a counterclaim (Art. 33(3) UPCA)
An action for a declaration of non-infringement is stayed if an infringement action is brought within three months (Art. 33(6) UPCA)
distinction:d_upc_lokalkammer_zentralkam.merksatz: Attack on the product to the local division, attack on the patent to the central division – unless the local division is already seised.

distinction:d_upc_hauptsache_einstweilig.label: Infringement action vs. application for provisional measures
distinction:d_upc_hauptsache_einstweilig.frage: How do main proceedings and summary proceedings before the UPC differ?
rows: Art. 32(1)(a), Art. 63 ff. UPCA; R. 12 to 118 RoP
Art. 32(1)(c), Art. 62 UPCA; R. 205 to 213 RoP
Full conviction of the Court after taking of evidence; burden of proof on the party relying on the fact (Art. 54 UPCA)
Sufficient degree of certainty = more likely than not (R. 211.2 RoP; NanoString/10x)
Only by way of Counterclaim for revocation (R. 25 RoP); options under Art. 33(3) UPCA
Defence without a separate action; burden of proof on the respondent; can be waived at any time (Merz/Viatris)
None
Unreasonable delay is detrimental (R. 211.4 RoP); it must not be possible to await the main proceedings (Biolitec)
Always a written procedure with a defence (three months)
Rule: hearing; exceptionally ex parte (R. 212 RoP) with a duty of disclosure (R. 206.4 RoP)
Aim: oral hearing within one year; interim procedure
A few weeks to months; decision by the panel or a single judge
Two months, final decision (R. 220.1(a) RoP)
15 days, order under Art. 62 UPCA (R. 220.1(c) RoP)
Setting aside has retroactive effect; penalty payments lapse (Kodak/Fujifilm)
No-fault liability for damages (Art. 62(5) UPCA, R. 213.2 RoP); security (R. 211.5 RoP)
distinction:d_upc_hauptsache_einstweilig.merksatz: Summary proceedings = probability instead of certainty, speed instead of completeness, security instead of res judicata.

distinction:d_upc_r262_r262a.label: Third-party access to the file (R. 262 RoP) vs. protection of confidential information (R. 262A RoP)
distinction:d_upc_r262_r262a.frage: When does R. 262 RoP apply, and when R. 262A RoP?
spalten: R. 262 RoP (public access to the register)
rows: Public access to decisions (automatic) and to written pleadings/evidence (on reasoned request, R. 262.1(b) RoP)
Restriction of access by the other party and its representatives to a specific circle of persons
Third party (represented under Art. 48 UPCA) or a party for a confidentiality request (R. 262.2 RoP)
The party lodging the document
At any time; decision by the judge-rapporteur after hearing the parties
When lodging the document (R. 262A.3 RoP)
Reasoned interest of the third party (including a law firm's abstract interest in training, Huawei/MediaTek); confidentiality interests
Applicant's interest significantly outweighs (R. 262A.5 RoP); right to a fair trial; at least one natural person per party (Ericsson/ASUS)
None: an application under R. 262.2 RoP does not protect against disclosure by the other party; the secret is lost (EOFlow/Insulet)
Yes: restriction of access, continues to apply beyond the instance (Curio/10x)
Review under R. 333 RoP, then appeal under R. 220.2, 220.3 RoP (UPC CoA 2026)
Appeal under R. 220.2, 220.3 RoP
distinction:d_upc_r262_r262a.merksatz: R. 262 RoP governs what the world sees; R. 262A RoP governs what the opponent sees.

distinction:d_upc_einspruch_klageerwider.label: Preliminary objection (R. 19 RoP) vs. Statement of defence (R. 23 RoP)
distinction:d_upc_einspruch_klageerwider.frage: What belongs in the Preliminary objection, and what in the Statement of defence?
kriterien: Effect on the main time limit
rows: One month from service of the Statement of claim (R. 19.1 RoP)
Three months from service (R. 23 RoP)
Only: jurisdiction of the Court (including opt-out), competence of the division, language of the Statement of claim; exhaustive (Roku/Dolby)
All defences on the merits: non-infringement, limitations, exhaustion, FRAND; invalidity only by way of counterclaim (R. 25 RoP)
Acceptance of jurisdiction (R. 19.7 RoP); objection excluded on appeal (Sinocare/Abbott)
Decision by default (R. 355 RoP) at the claimant's request
Judge-rapporteur, where appropriate referral to the main proceedings (R. 20 RoP); referral to the competent division (R. 19.5 RoP)
Panel in the final decision
Appeal under R. 21 RoP (if rejected, only with leave under R. 220.2 RoP); stay only once an appeal has been lodged (Sun Patent/Vivo)
Appeal against the final decision (R. 220.1(a) RoP)
Does not affect the time limit for the Statement of defence (R. 19.6 RoP), unless the judge-rapporteur decides otherwise
Extension only in exceptional cases (R. 9.3 RoP), for instance where annexes are missing (Sanofi/Amgen)
distinction:d_upc_einspruch_klageerwider.merksatz: The Preliminary objection asks “may this court hear the case?”, the Statement of defence asks “is the claimant right?”.

distinction:d_upc_berufung_entscheidung_.label: Appeal against final decisions vs. against orders
distinction:d_upc_berufung_entscheidung_.frage: Which decisions of the Court of First Instance can be challenged, and how?
rows: Decision on the merits (including the decision on the principle of costs), decision ending the proceedings, decision by default
Orders under Art. 49(5), 59, 60, 61, 62, 67 UPCA
Case management orders, value of the dispute, order imposing a penalty payment (EOFlow/Insulet), decisions under R. 333 RoP
None
None
Leave by the Court of First Instance or discretionary review by the standing judge (R. 220.3, 220.4 RoP)
Two months from service of the reasoned decision (R. 224.1(a) RoP)
15 days (R. 224.1(b) RoP)
15 days from leave, or application for review within 15 days
No, except revocation decisions (Art. 74(2) UPCA); application under R. 223 RoP
No; application under R. 223 RoP
No (R. 223.5 RoP)
Judgment on infringement and counterclaim
Provisional measure, order to preserve evidence, change of language
Extension of a time limit, confidentiality order, access to the file
distinction:d_upc_berufung_entscheidung_.merksatz: Final decisions and urgent orders can be appealed freely; everything else needs leave.

distinction:d_upc_beweissicherung_beweis.label: Order to preserve evidence (Art. 60 UPCA) vs. order to produce evidence (Art. 59 UPCA)
distinction:d_upc_beweissicherung_beweis.frage: When an order to preserve evidence/inspection, and when an order to produce evidence?
spalten: Order to preserve evidence and inspection (Art. 60 UPCA, R. 192 ff. RoP)
Order to produce evidence (Art. 59 UPCA, R. 190 RoP)
rows: Preservation of evidence at risk, inspection of premises, taking of samples (“saisie”)
Production of specified evidence in the control of the other party or third parties
Before or during the main proceedings; often ex parte
In pending proceedings, typically in the interim procedure
Reasonably available evidence, plausibility of infringement; no fishing expedition (Centripetal/Palo Alto)
Substantiated, relevant and disputed facts; no exploration of unknown facts (LD Düsseldorf Ecovacs/Roborock)
Carried out by a court-appointed expert (R. 196.4, 196.5 RoP); restriction on use (R. 196.2 RoP)
Order with conditions, protection of confidentiality (R. 262A RoP)
Alleged infringer, where appropriate third parties
Other party or third party
Security (Art. 60(7) UPCA), damages if set aside (Art. 60(9) UPCA), review (R. 197.3 RoP), time limit for starting main proceedings (Art. 60(8) UPCA, R. 198.1 RoP)
Right to be heard before the order; confidentiality (Art. 58 UPCA)
distinction:d_upc_beweissicherung_beweis.merksatz: Art. 60 UPCA secures evidence before it disappears; Art. 59 UPCA obtains evidence the opponent holds.

distinction:d_upc_epg_deutsches_verfahre.label: Infringement proceedings before the UPC vs. before German courts
distinction:d_upc_epg_deutsches_verfahre.frage: What is different before the UPC compared with German patent infringement proceedings?
rows: Counterclaim for revocation possible before the same division (Art. 33(3)(a) UPCA); bifurcation only as an option
Bifurcation principle: revocation action only before the BPatG (§ 81 PatG); the infringement court may at most stay the proceedings (§ 148 ZPO)
All Contracting Member States for which the patent has effect (Art. 34 UPCA)
Only the German part of the European patent
Front-loaded, fixed time limits, oral hearing within about one year; three stages of proceedings
Statement of claim, defence, reply, rejoinder within time limits set by the court; hearing usually after 12 to 15 months
Multinational panel, technically qualified judge from the pool
Three professional judges without technical training; court experts
Optional: German or English before German local divisions; language of the patent on request
German (§ 184 GVG)
Fixed fee plus value-based fee, reimbursement up to the ceiling (Art. 69 UPCA)
GKG fees based on the value of the dispute, reimbursement at RVG rates (§ 91 ZPO)
Immediately enforceable, penalty payment imposed by the Court itself (R. 354 RoP)
Provisional enforceability against security (§ 709 ZPO), coercive measures under § 890 ZPO
Appeal to the Court of Appeal in Luxembourg, no third instance; referral to the CJEU
Appeal to the OLG, complaint against denial of leave to appeal on points of law/appeal on points of law to the BGH
distinction:d_upc_epg_deutsches_verfahre.merksatz: The UPC combines infringement and validity in one set of proceedings with effect for the entire territory of the Contracting Member States – that is the systemic break with Germany.
